text.p: Petro-Canada said on Wednesday it agreed to swap all of its interests in the Scotian Shelf off Canada's east coast for some of Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada's western Canadian oil and gas properties.

The deal, in which talks were confirmed in early June, will see Petro-Canada swap its 18-percent stake in the Sable Offshore Energy Project as well as remaining interests off the coast of Nova Scotia.
Mobil is currently operator and 41 percent owner of the C$2-billion Sable project, which still requires final approval.
In return, Petro-Canada will boost its interest in the Ferrier Cardium Unit No. 3 oil property in west-central Alberta to 99 percent from 57 percent.
It will also acquire Mobil's interests in some producing natural gas fields at Gilby and Notikewan as well as exploration acreage at Ricinus.
Petro-Canada said its incremental daily output from the fields is expected to be about 2,300 barrels of oil and natural gas liquids and 15 million cubic feet of natural gas.
The properties' proved developed reserves were estimated at about 12 million barrels of oil and liquids and 40 billion cubic feet of gas.

"Petro-Canada will receive current oil and gas production, along with attractive exploration acreage, within its core areas of operations in Western Canada," Petro-Canada executive vice-president Norm McIntyre said in a statement.
"Off the east coast of Canada, we will be able to focus specifically on developing our substantial oil reserves offshore Newfoundland."
Jerry Anderson, president and general manager of Mobil Canada, said the move, which boosts his company's Sable interest to 59 percent, is aimed at solidifying Mobil's position on the Scotian Shelf.
"We have been working to restructure our western Canadian business, getting out of high-risk, high cost exploration and seeling off or managing differently non-strategic properties," Anderson said.
"This trade meets our needs by exchanging non-strategic western Canadian properties for strategic eastern Canadian properties."
Mobil said the assets it swapped contributed less than three percent of its total western Canadian output.
Anderson said he expected Mobil Canada to be producing 100,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from the Canadian offshore.

The companies said the deal, which still required due diligence and regulatory approval, would be effective July 1, 1996. Closing was expected before the end of this year. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
